summary:
Astervox is an interactive 3D world atlas web application designed to explore global geography alongside historical climate and environmental data. Using an interactive globe with search, border, cloud, and daylight toggles, users can examine multi-decade trends—such as shifts in air temperature, moisture in the air, wind speed, and soil wetness—via trend charts, statistical confidence indicators, and year-by-year timeline playback. The platform also pairs country-level facts with a deep-data drill-down feature that retrieves NASA POWER climate parameters for specific cities, streets, or coordinates.
Navigating raw climate and geospatial datasets across different scales and timeframes can be overwhelming. Astervox addresses this challenge by uniting visual globe exploration, historical trend analysis, and localized environmental metrics in a single interface. By turning complex Earth observation data into an accessible, interactive experience, Astervox makes it easier for users to understand how environmental conditions change over time across both broad regions and specific locations.
details:
Astervox is an interactive 3D globe that shows how Earth’s climate has changed since 1981 using NASA data. Users can zoom from the full planet down to country, city, and local scales. It displays temperature, humidity, soil moisture, wind, precipitation, and other climate variables with long-term trends and year-by-year animation.

Benefits: Makes complex NASA climate data easy to explore and understand for anyone.

Impact: Helps people see climate change as a local reality, not just a global average.

Technologies: React, Redux, Three.js, Tailwind CSS, Vite, NASA POWER API (MERRA-2 + CERES), Natural Earth data.

Creativity: Progressive zoom that reveals more detail (cities, oceans, local climate) as you get closer, combined with beautiful 3D Earth and rigorous climate analysis in one simple browser app.
